concepts.def: Processes instructions via the fetch–decode–execute cycle.
Stores data and instructions in the same memory.
RAM is volatile working memory; ROM is permanent.
Fast memory close to the CPU for frequently used data.
Tiny, fast stores inside the CPU (e.g. the accumulator).
How many cycles the CPU performs per second.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Computer Architecture — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computer Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computer Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: It can explode or be damaged easily.
Its contents are lost when power is removed.
It can store data permanently.
IP is for input, MAC is for output.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Trace table”?
options: Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Abstraction”?
options: Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
